what: The catalog gives the create-judo-project goal and its parameters but not the plugin groupId or version. The builder took version 1.0.0.20260311 from ~/.m2, which then pulled template 1.0.0.20261109 from judo-ng.
why: Build-process section lists parameters only. Plugin coordinates and a version pin are not documented, so the builder guessed from the local Maven cache.
workaround: Used the locally cached plugin version found under ~/.m2/repository/hu/blackbelt/judo.

what: The CLI doc says the judo-cli.jar is downloaded by ./judo.sh build. In this generated project, generate-root did not create target/judo-cli.jar. Running mvn -DgenerateRoot validate did.
why: The catalog describes the download as part of judo.sh build. The generated root pom has its own download-cli profile that runs on generateRoot, so the catalog is incomplete for the new-project case.
workaround: Ran mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate, which copied target/judo-cli.jar.

what: Mapping a TransferObjectType to an entity made the CLI auto-create members, forms, tables and views. The builder's hand-added DataMembers then failed validate --strict with binding and uniqueness errors.
why: The catalog does not say that a mapped TransferObjectType creates its members and UI scaffolds, so the builder assumed it had to create them.
workaround: Discarded the unsaved edits and rebuilt the model without the hand-added MAPPED members.

what: No documented recipe for the first login user of a local dev app: no test user, no seed data and no credentials are given for the generated Keycloak realm.
why: Grep of agent-docs found only integration-test users and the test realm file. The local-development doc has no login step. The builder had to create a Keycloak user and a DB row by hand.
workaround: Created Keycloak user shop/shop through the admin REST API and inserted a t_webshop_shop_user row with psql. Wrapped in scripts/seed-dev-user.sh.

what: local-development.md gives the app URL as http://localhost:8181/apps/. The app is at /webshop/Shop/, and /apps/ only lists bundles.
why: Doc is out of date for the generated app path.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8181/webshop/Shop/ (from the Karaf start log).

what: Keycloak on the local port is served under /auth (Keycloak 23 with a relative path). Root and /realms return 404, and the catalog gives http://localhost:8080 with no path.
why: judo.sh starts Keycloak with --http-relative-path /auth, which the local-development doc does not mention.
workaround: Used http://localhost:8280/auth for admin and realm calls.

what: The generated judo.properties sets dbtype=hsqldb, but local-development.md says the default run uses PostgreSQL in Docker.
why: Doc and generated default disagree.
workaround: Changed dbtype to postgresql in judo.properties.

what: The predefined Text type is limited to 250 characters, which is too short for a product description. The catalog does not say so and does not name a long-text type.
why: Type doc lists StringType widget properties but not the Text length limit.
workaround: Added StringType LongText with maxLength 4000 in webshop::types.

what: No model-level way to show a price with two decimals in the generated table. The table shows 89.9 and 129.5.
why: The generated table valueFormatter uses Intl.NumberFormat with defaults. formatValue exists in the model but the table column does not set fraction digits.
workaround: Patched the generated table component (see c01-21).

what: The table column customizer example in table-hooks.md uses a (original) => ... signature and registration that do not match the shipped type, which is () => ColumnCustomizer.
why: Docs out of date against utilities/table.ts in the generated app.
workaround: Not used. Builder edited generated code instead.

what: The frontend uses a hash router. Pages open at /webshop/Shop/#/Shop/Products/..., so direct paths without the hash return 404. The catalog does not mention this.
why: Frontend docs do not describe the router type or the URL shape.
workaround: Used hash URLs (for example #/Shop/Products/AccessTablePage).

what: The REST contract for updates and lists is not documented: the paths under /api/webshop/Shop/Shop/..., the X-Judo-SignedIdentifier and X-Judo-Mask headers, and the ~list and ~update verbs.
why: Builder had to read the generated frontend services to find the update path and headers.
workaround: Read ProductInfoServiceImpl.ts and headers.ts, then called REST with curl.

what: The generated table does not open the view page on a row click in a way the builder could find. The only row-click doc was the e2e test helper, and the embedded table row view button applies to references.
why: The catalog has no section on how a TransferObjectTable opens its view page (rowOperations versus row click).
workaround: Used a DOM eval to click the grid cell, which opened the view page.

what: validate --strict failed with ExposedTransferObjectTableHasColumns (no columns on the viewable table). The fix was the fill command, which the builder found by trial.
why: The accesspoint doc states the rule, but the fill command is not in the judo-cli reference (openspec sweep item MO-172 lists it as missing).
workaround: fill webshop::ProductInfo --pages view,form,table.

what: The kb says to re-fetch the judo-cli.jar with ./mvnw -f application/model/pom.xml -N validate, but the project has no mvnw wrapper. The command failed with exit 127.
why: Catalog gives a wrapper command that the generated project does not ship. Plain mvn also did not fetch the jar; the root-pom profile route (mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate) worked.
workaround: Used mvn -B -DgenerateRoot validate to fetch target/judo-cli.jar.

what: ./judo.sh generate runs a clean that deletes target/judo-cli.jar. Every model edit made through the CLI jar after a generate fails with 'Unable to access jarfile'.
why: Generate wipes the target folder, and the jar lives there. The required order (fetch jar, change model, save, then generate and build) is not documented as a single sequence.
workaround: Re-fetched the jar before each model change and ran generate and build after the model was saved.

what: Builder's GAPS entry says the table-hooks.md column customizer example documents TABLE_COLUMN_CUSTOMIZER_HOOK_INTERFACE_KEY with {component, column} but does not say the hook works only when the DataColumn has customImplementation=true in the model.
why: Builder's reading of the doc; the doc lacks the model precondition.

what: The table-hooks.md column customizer example shows the hook as (original) => ..., but the shipped type is () => (original) => GridColDef, a factory that returns the transform. The builder logged the difference.
why: The catalog example signature does not match the shipped ColumnCustomizerHook type.
workaround: Followed the shipped type in the notes; the hook itself could not be used (see c02-04).

what: Builder states the catalog has no hook for a view or field display; ui-hooks.md covers only AppBar, hero, logo, footer and menu. The only route it found is a model-level custom implementation on the field.
why: ui-hooks.md scope does not list field or detail display hooks, so a price display on a plain DataField has no documented hook.
workaround: Used the model customImplementation flag on the form and view price fields.

what: Titles and menus still show internal names: 'ProductInfo Table', 'ProductInfo View / Edit', and the phone bottom bar shows 'ProductInfo' and 'Other'. Orchestrator requires user-facing labels 'Products' and 'Product'.
why: Model labels still carry the entity name; the builder had not set labels or i18n for the pages, menu and bottom bar.
workaround: Round 3 task: fix labels via model label and/or i18n, as the kb documents.

what: Phone bottom bar 'Other' label comes from the i18n key menuTree.other with default 'Other' in the generated BottomMenu. The kb has no section on it, so the builder read the generated source to find it.
why: Bottom-bar overflow label is a hard-coded i18n default that the catalog does not document.
workaround: Round 3: add an i18n override for menuTree.other via a generator override fragment (see c02-43).

what: Path and format of an i18n extra fragment for application_default.json were not in the kb. The builder first wrote the fragment under ui-react/actor/public/i18n with an unbraced JSON line, then found from the template jar that the path is actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs.
why: Best-practice page i18n-generator-override-extra-fragment.md says the path is project practice and not covered by agent-docs; the kb search did not return the template path.
workaround: Moved the fragment to application/frontend-react/generator-overrides/ui-react/actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs (override dir from the frontend pom), removed the wrong folders and rebuilt; menuTree.other became 'More' in application_en-US.json.

what: The kb has no section that says where the generated order of form and view fields comes from. The builder had to read the esm2ui transformation jar to learn it.
why: Catalog gap: the order rule (position from the container components in the ESM model) is not in the kb; the 'move' section of judo-cli.md does not say it affects generated field order.
workaround: Read the tatami esm2ui ETL (esmToUi.etl) from the local jar.

what: A custom view layout cannot be made from a placeholder: a ui:Placeholder marked customImplementation generates no scaffold and renders nothing. The builder then removed the price and description fields, and the details page showed empty price and description, because the generated view only loads attributes that have a field.
why: Catalog gives no documented hook for replacing a whole view; the placeholder route does not render, and the field-based data load is not documented.
workaround: Kept all three view fields as custom implementations; only the name component renders the full layout, the price and description components render nothing.

what: After the view fields were removed, regeneration dropped the view's .default scaffold, but the builder's copied register file stayed in src/custom. The frontend build then failed (TS2305 missing export from the customization module, TS2322 type mismatch).
why: A hand-copied scaffold is not removed by generate; the catalog does not say what happens to a copied scaffold when its element disappears.
workaround: Rewrote the register file by hand for the remaining custom elements and rebuilt.

what: The generated dashboard page already renders a ComponentProxy for the custom visual element key DashboardPage, with a Hello! fallback. A service registered under that key replaces the home page. The kb does not describe this seam; the builder found it by reading generated code.
why: Catalog only covers a dashboard without layout (component-proxy-placeholder-page.md, project practice) and Extra Routes; the generated seam for the dashboard is not documented.
workaround: Registered CatalogHome via src/custom/hooks/registerCatalogHome.tsx from application-customizer.tsx (already generator-ignored); no generated file touched.

what: No documented empty-data route for the product grid, so the empty-state Playwright check could not be run as a real user action. The test is skipped and logged.
why: Catalog documents no way to force an empty list for a generated service without a data change.
workaround: Test skipped; logged as GAPS R5-4.

what: Validator error AllRequiredFeaturesHaveBindingIfCreatable: a transfer object used by a create operation excludes required features (ProductInfo lacked sku and unit).
why: Required features on a create-used transfer object must be bound (MAPPED) to the entity; builder had not added them.
workaround: Added MAPPED DataMembers sku and unit with binding to Product features, then validate passed.

what: Validator error AggregationOnBothSidesAreNotAllowed (circular aggregation) on the mapped one-way relations ProductInfo.category and CategoryInfo.products, which the CLI created with relationKind AGGREGATION by default.
why: Both ends of the pair defaulted to AGGREGATION; builder did not know the default or the rule for one-way mapped relations.
workaround: Set both relationKind to ASSOCIATION so validate passed; later set ProductInfo.category back to AGGREGATION (only one side) to get the autocomplete form widget.

what: judo create -t MenuItemAccess is refused: the menu item access is created automatically with the actor access.
why: Menu item accesses are generated by the Designer cascade, not by a direct create command.
workaround: Used create -t Access on the actor and let the cascade create the menu item.

what: Validator warned: columns are not defined for a viewable table with a target on ProductInfo.category.
why: A relation feature on a table needs its columns defined; builder had not yet defined them.
workaround: Added name column to the category relation in the form and view.

what: Seed test failed with a 500: column t02.c_sku does not exist in the persistent PostgreSQL database after SKU was added to the model.
why: A stored member added to a persistent database needs a schema-upgrade; the builder assumed the generated changelog would apply to the existing volume.
workaround: Builder removed the postgres and keycloak containers and volumes, restarted, and reseeded the dev user.

what: Playwright fill() on the generated text field did not store the value; the create dialog stayed open and Create was never accepted. Stored data then failed with MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE on categories create.
why: Generated inputs store the value on blur or on real key events, not on programmatic fill().
workaround: Used pressSequentially with a blur after each field.

what: Builder tried representationComponent link, autocomplete and tag on the category relation; the CLI accepted only table (then button after relationKind changed). The catalog lists table, button and tag for to-one relations.
why: Allowed representationComponent values depend on relationKind as enforced by the CLI, which the catalog's shape table does not state clearly; the builder guessed values before reading the catalog.
workaround: Set relationKind to AGGREGATION on ProductInfo.category, then set representationComponent to table on Form and View_Edit.

what: Relation widget on the product form rendered as a link button; the builder wanted a dropdown picker for the category and found that a dropdown is a separate widget (isTypeAheadField/autocompleteRows), not a representationComponent value.
why: The mapping of to-one relation to widget is split across attributes and the catalog pages disagree on which values apply.
workaround: Kept the table representation and used the existing relation selector in the form.

what: Table filters defaulted to labels such as NameFilter, so the test could not find the Name filter in the menu.
why: The DataFilter label is not set by default from the attribute; the catalog does not say so.
workaround: Set labels Name, SKU, Unit and Price (number) on the filters with update -s label=.

what: kb_search for eager or isEager and embedded tables on views returned generic embedded-table sections; the view-table example (TabularReferenceField with representationComponent=table) was only found by grep, and no isEager attribute exists in the catalog.
why: The orchestrator's term isEager is not a catalog concept; the catalog answer is the to-many TabularReferenceField on the view, which the search did not rank first.
workaround: Read the catalog by grep, then used a to-many TabularReferenceField with representationComponent table on the view.

what: Builder noted that the CLI lists table, button, tag and card as valid representationComponent values for a to-many relation, while the catalog shape table lists table, card and tag only.
why: Possible mismatch between the catalog shape table and the CLI schema for to-many relations.

what: Builder noted that an image stored as a binary attribute cannot be used as a plain img src, because the download needs the token header; the catalog says to use a binary-to-object-URL hook.
why: Catalog states the download path is a separate authenticated request and marks the src behaviour as verify for the generated version.
workaround: Planned to use the object-URL hook for image display, with a placeholder when there is no image.

what: Transfer objects created with a mapping (VariantInfo, AddressInfo, AdminAccountInfo) already had mapped members; adding the same members again gave BindingIsNotMappedByOtherMappedAttribute and NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer errors. Adding a label feature that is not placeable also failed.
why: Creating a TransferObjectType with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members; the builder's script added them a second time. The CLI reference does not say so.
workaround: Deleted the duplicate DataMembers and kept the auto-created ones.

what: Creating an actor with a principal auto-creates a Claim per attribute (for example Customer email USERNAME and EMAIL); the builder removed the USERNAME claim so only EMAIL remains.
why: The principal and claim cascade in the CLI creates claims by default; the catalog does not say which claim to keep.
workaround: Deleted the USERNAME claim on Customer.

what: After generate alone the new webshop__customer and webshop__admin modules had no src/custom folder; it appeared only after the build. The catalog does not say when src/custom is created.
why: Generation creates the module shell; the custom folder and hook scaffolds come from the build step, which the catalog does not state.
workaround: Read the generated tree; no custom code moved yet; decision deferred to the frontend step.

what: The model has no setting for Keycloak self sign-up (registrationAllowed); the generated realm JSON leaves it unset, so the builder had to set it through the Keycloak admin API.
why: The platform's generated realm does not expose a self sign-up switch in the documented model settings; catalog does not cover it.
workaround: Logged as GAPS R7-3; the seed script switches self sign-up on through the Keycloak admin API.

what: Generated actor modules (webshop__admin, webshop__customer) each get their own e2e module; the Level 0 Playwright tests had to be split across them by hand (git mv).
why: Each actor has its own generated e2e and frontend module; the catalog does not say how existing tests move between them.
workaround: Moved helpers and specs to the matching module, changed the base URL to Admin or Customer, and added actor-specific login helpers.

what: Variants and addresses inside a product or profile view are saved only with the page Update button; the tests failed until they clicked Update.
why: Composed child rows belong to the parent view and are stored with the parent save; the catalog does not say so next to the inline table pattern.
workaround: Tests click Update (saveView, saveProfile) after adding the child rows.

what: Interceptor provisioned a CustomerAccount row for admin@example.com because the admin user also logs in through the customer client; the decision was made on the client argument and the token azp had to be used instead.
why: The client argument passed to AuthenticationInterceptor is not the client id the builder expected; the catalog does not say what it contains.
workaround: Read the azp claim, logged the origin, and returned early for non-customer clients; a stray admin row was then removed.

what: A customer who opens the back office URL gets a User not found page instead of an access message.
why: The expected error for a wrong actor is not described in the catalog as far as the builder reported.
workaround: Reported as a known behaviour in the round report; no test change.

what: Category filter test on the product table was marked test.fail() in Round 6 because a relation cannot be a top-level table column or filter without a derived attribute.
why: Catalog says a RelationColumn on a top-level table is a codegen bug; a flattened derived attribute is the documented route.
workaround: Marked test.fail() with reason; the Round 7 F12 derived categoryName removed the fail and added the filter.

what: The generated layout stores the mini drawer state in browser storage (webshop-config) and recomputes it only when the window crosses a size tier, so a browser that was once small opens collapsed on a desktop screen, also after reload.
why: Behaviour not described in the catalog; the builder searched the kb twice and found nothing on drawer state.
workaround: Render-nothing DrawerExpander registered as the documented AppBar extra component opens the drawer at lg and xl widths on load and on size change, in both actors.
proposed_target: generated layout drawer (miniDrawer persistence); document the workaround in ui-hooks.md

what: Admin product table columns needed fixed widths at 1440 px, but the builder did not know the unit or value format of DataColumn.width and set plain integers (170, 120, 100 and so on).
why: The CLI schema shows width as a plain string; the catalog says fixed pixel width but the builder did not find a value example for the attribute.
workaround: Plain integer widths set on every column; all columns and row actions fit at 1440 and the admin tests now run at 1440.
